findings.what: The claraWork_v4 successor-contract stanza's refusal map for ask_knowledge_conflict names a reason 'invalid_question_fields' for the CLR10 field-validation case. clara.open_work_question (0180_work_questions.sql) never raises that reason -- every field-shape refusal in _assert_work_question_fields (0180:316-402) carries detail.reason = 'invalid_fields' (with a 'field'/'constraint' pair), never 'invalid_question_fields'. The brief requires this stanza's refusal map to be complete and correct so the integration worker can cut claraWork_v4 directly from it; as written it points at a code path that does not exist.
findings.evidence: 0180_work_questions.sql:59 ('CLR10 invalid_fields + field + constraint') and :317-402 (ten literal detail=jsonb_build_object('reason','invalid_fields',...) sites) vs 654-final.md:68 ('CLR10 `invalid_question_fields` -> terminal author error'). No occurrence of the string 'invalid_question_fields' exists anywhere in 0180 (grep confirmed).
findings.fix: Correct the refusal-map line to 'CLR10 invalid_fields (field/constraint identifies which)' before this stanza is cut into claraWork_v4, so the integration worker maps the real door reason rather than a fabricated one.

findings.what: The walk never calls page.emulateMedia({reducedMotion:'reduce'}), so AC5's reduced-motion state is untested for the promote dialog and the firm register. Not a regression introduced by #654: #644's own knowledge-walk.spec.ts (same shared ArApCounterpartyDoorDialog composition) also has zero reducedMotion coverage, so #654 follows the established pattern for this dialog family rather than dropping new coverage.
findings.evidence: grep -c reducedMotion apps/web/e2e/knowledge-firm-walk.spec.ts apps/web/e2e/knowledge-walk.spec.ts -> 0 in both files, versus e2e/chat-parity-walk.spec.ts, journal-work-walk.spec.ts, checkout-gate-walk.spec.ts etc. which do call page.emulateMedia({reducedMotion:'reduce'}).
findings.fix: Add one emulateMedia({reducedMotion:'reduce'}) leg to the promote-dialog open/close test, following e2e/chat-parity-walk.spec.ts's pattern -- worth doing once for both knowledge specs together rather than as a #654-only fix.

findings.what: One flaky failure was observed and independently reproduced as host contention, exactly the pattern this review's instructions warn about: 'the firm register now shows the rule with the authority the act recorded...' timed out on page.goto after 30s (net::ERR_ABORTED / frame detached) on the full-suite run, then passed in 5.3s on an isolated re-run of just knowledge-firm-walk.spec.ts (11/11 clean, no other change). The worker's own report already flags this class of risk.
findings.evidence: Full-suite run: 'x 4 ... the firm register now shows the rule ... (35.3s)' with 'Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded. Error: page.goto: net::ERR_ABORTED; maybe frame was detached?'. Isolated re-run of the same spec immediately after: '11 passed (1.3m)', that test at 5.3s. 654-final.md:94 already states 'the first two runs of the new spec failed on my own fixture and assertion errors ... not on flake' -- this run's failure is a third, host-contention-shaped failure mode distinct from those two.
findings.fix: No action needed; treat a lone page.goto ERR_ABORTED timeout on this spec on this shared host as a re-run candidate before treating it as a real regression.
